text:
support-jen: ACME reported intermittent 500s and streaming cutoffs at ~17:12 UTC. They saw body: 'response ended unexpectedly' and lots of retries.
oncall-dan: looking... any repro? which model/pool?
support-jen: hosted-prod pool 'gpustream-3', model: redwood-openxl-13b-q4, dynbatch recently bumped to 64 (was 32). sample curl from customer:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"model":"openxl-13b","input":"<long streaming prompt>","stream":true}'
```
ops-bot: alert: upstream worker exit (SIGSEGV) on host gpu-3f: container restart count=3
infra-liu: grabbed logs from gpu-3f, see NVML OOM + segfaults. snippet:
```
E tensorflow: out of memory (CUDA) device 0: requested 1.2GB, available 512MB
F libc: Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7ff... ip=0x4f2a1
```
kevin: stacktrace suggests runtime crashed inside attention kernel when batch size jumped. dynbatch=64 likely increased per-step memory.
sre-maria: repro steps I ran with internal load generator: steady qps 120, request ctx 30k tokens, dynbatch 64 -> worker mem balloon -> cgroup OOM killer log before sigsegv.
kevin: can you paste `nvidia-smi` right after repro? also /var/log/messages and `dmesg` show gpu reset.
infra-liu: nvidia-smi after crash:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        | Memory-Usage |
| 0   A100          On          | 0000:3b:00.0  | 9830MiB / 40536MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
support-jen: customer impact: ~30% of their requests in the window returned 500; they want ETA and mitigation.
oncall-dan: immediate mitigations: 1) revert dynbatch to 32 on gpustream-3 pool 2) evict and drain any unhealthy workers 3) add fallback route to smaller model variant 4) open CS update to ACME.
kevin: created runtime patch candidate to cap per-request batch multiply; rolling it to canary now.
sre-maria: short-term patch applied: dynbatch cap=40 for gpustream-3; restarted pool, monitoring p95 tail.
ops-bot: deploy: canary to gpustream-3-dynbatch-caps succeeded. respawned 12/12.
infra-liu: follow-ups: - add KV cache guard to avoid mem spike for long ctx - add stress test for dynbatch scale with large-token clients - create alert when container restarts > 2 in 5m
support-jen: CS message drafted: "We observed a memory regression with recent dynamic batching that caused upstream worker restarts; we've applied a cap and are monitoring. We'll follow up with a log bundle and config changes." :thumbsup:
kevin: logs & repro notes pushed to incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-2026-1745559999
sre-maria: assigning follow-ups to infra-liu (stress tests), kevin (runtime guard), oncall-dan (postmortem) — target EOD tomorrow.
oncall-dan: will update when p95 stable <300ms and no restarts in 30m.
support-jen: ACME replied thanks, asks for timeline for permanent fix.
kevin: ETA for runtime guard: 48-72 hours. I'll include clear rollback plan.
ops-bot: NOTE: automated snapshot of container logs and GPU coredump uploaded to /artifacts/INC-1745559999
